query: Consider the following context: High entropy alloys have excellent wear resistance, so they have great application prospects in the fields of wear resistance and surface protection. In that context, which material can be used for adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Using a Ni-based interlayer to mediate the deposition of an AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy coating onto a copper substrate improves the metallurgical bonding and wear resistance of the composite compared to directly depositing the alloy on copper.
generation.material_initial_state: A Cu matrix with a clean, pre-treated surface, prone to poor adhesion with high entropy alloys.
generation.intervention: Introduce a Ni interlayer via techniques such as arc spraying or laser cladding, followed by deposition of an AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy coating.
generation.conditions: Deposition should be conducted under controlled thermal conditions to manage mismatches in thermal expansion and promote metallurgical bonding between layers.
generation.structural_mediator: The Ni interlayer forms solid solutions with both the Cu substrate and the high entropy alloy, reducing thermal expansion mismatch and enhancing adhesion.
generation.mechanism: The Ni interlayer acts as a chemical bridge between Cu and the high entropy alloy, facilitating metallurgical bonding and reducing stress concentrations at the interface, which in turn results in improved wear resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: The composite system will exhibit a robust metallurgical bond and significantly enhanced wear resistance relative to a Cu substrate with a directly deposited high entropy alloy coating.
generation.baseline: A Cu substrate with a directly-deposited high entropy alloy coating typically shows weak bonding and inferior wear resistance due to poor interfacial compatibility.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies specifically to systems where a Ni interlayer is feasible; alternative interlayer materials or deposition techniques may not yield similar improvements.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal thickness and deposition parameters for the Ni interlayer and the quantitative degree of wear resistance improvement require further experimental determination.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three sets of samples: (1) Cu substrate with directly deposited AlCoCrFeNi coating, (2) Cu substrate with a Ni interlayer then the AlCoCrFeNi coating, and (3) Cu substrate with a different interlayer (or no interlayer) as a control. Use identical deposition parameters for the alloy layer. Assess interfacial bonding and wear resistance for all samples.
measurements: Perform metallurgical cross-sectional analysis using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) to evaluate the interfacial bonding.
Quantitatively measure adhesion strength using standardized peel or scratch tests.
Conduct wear resistance tests under identical load and sliding conditions to measure wear rates and track the coefficient of friction.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If samples with the Ni interlayer do not show a statistically significant improvement in interfacial bonding (as measured by adhesion tests and microstructural integrity) and wear resistance over those without it, the hypothesis will be falsified.

recalled_precedents.study: Liu et al. (circa 2015) on laser cladding of AlCoCrFeNi high‐entropy alloy coatings on Cu substrates
recalled_precedents.approach: They applied a high‐energy laser cladding technique to deposit an AlCoCrFeNi coating directly onto copper, sometimes introducing intermediate treatments to enhance the metallurgical bonding between the dissimilar materials.
recalled_precedents.finding: The resultant coating exhibited a robust metallurgical bond with the Cu substrate and significantly improved wear resistance compared to bare copper.

recalled_precedents.study: Li et al. (circa 2016–2017) investigating the effect of Ni interlayers for high‐entropy alloy deposition on Cu
recalled_precedents.approach: This study employed a Ni-based transition layer between the Cu substrate and the high-entropy alloy coating, using methods such as arc spraying or cladding to deposit the layers sequentially.
recalled_precedents.finding: It was found that the Ni interlayer greatly improved adhesion by forming solid solutions with both copper and the high-entropy alloy, reducing thermal expansion mismatch and enhancing overall wear performance.
